Scaling experimentsshow a peak discovery quality factor of 0.83 with eight agents, supporting the prin-ciple that scientific AI should prioritize systematic refutation, causal identifiability,and machine-checkable proof.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202607.1126.v1\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026, 7, 15]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.1017/cbo9780511621123.003\", \"title\": [\"Falsification and the methodology of scientific research programmes\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9780511621123.003\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1978, 5, 18]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.7143760\", \"title\": [\"FalsiCite: Adaptive Falsification Agent for Traceable Miscitation Detection in Multimodal Scientific Literature\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>The rapid expansion of scientific publication has made citation verification at scale a critical but infeasible-to-manually-perform task. Existing large language model (LLM) based citation detectors suffer from two failure modes: hallucinated references, in which models confidently cite papers that do not exist or do not say what is claimed, and confirmation-cascade bias, in which an LLM judge tends to agree with its own prior verdicts even when those verdicts are wrong. Worse, real scientific claims are rarely supported by text alone; they draw on tables, figures, and equations scattered across the full paper, and naive modality fusion underperforms when modalities contribute unequally. We propose FalsiCite, an LLM-driven agent for traceable miscitation detection in multimodal scientific literature that unifies three innovations. First, an adaptive falsification verifier generates adversarial probes to actively disconfirm citation-claim alignments and updates a calibrated Bayesian posterior, explicitly countering confirmation-cascade bias. Second, a contribution-aware dynamic modality balance module estimates per-claim, per-modality contribution weights and reweights text, table, and figure features before fusion, mitigating modality laziness. Third, a weak-to-strong verification distillation scheme leverages visual in-context learning to scale verification capability from a small fine-tuned teacher to a large frontier student verifier without additional human labels. On the CiteME benchmark, FalsiCite achieves 74.6 percent accuracy and a 3.1 percent hallucination rate, outperforming the strongest prior agent (BibAgent, 72.4 percent) while producing a fully auditable reasoning trace. On the SciVer multimodal benchmark, FalsiCite attains 73.8 percent average accuracy, closing 21.5 percent of the gap between the strongest prior vision-language model and human experts. Human evaluation confirms that 91.7 percent of FalsiCite traces are fully grounded in retrievable evidence, compared to 76.4 percent for BibAgent and 51.2 percent for an LLM-as-a-Judge baseline. Ablations show that adaptive falsification reduces the confirmation-cascade failure rate from 19.7 percent to 5.4 percent, that modality balancing adds 4.6 accuracy points on multimodal claims, and that weak-to-strong distillation reduces annotation cost by an order of magnitude while preserving verifier quality.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7143760\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2026]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2514/6.2024-0047\", \"title\": [\"Agent-Based Discovery of Unexpected Falsification Scenarios in Aircraft Systems Virtual Testing\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2024-0047\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024, 1, 4]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "cb1b7c6aa61706c240fb918603a7d175fd2af65aee1d227351ffa002c3fb5934", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.20944/preprints202607.1126.v1", "doi:10.1017/cbo9780511621123.003", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.7143760", "doi:10.2514/6.2024-0047"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.20944/preprints202607.1126.v1", "https://doi.org/10.1017/cbo9780511621123.003", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7143760", "https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2024-0047"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
